<!--
Notes on this template — delete this comment in real entries.

FRONT MATTER IS THE TITLE ONLY. No `date`, `categories` or `description`: they
render as a "Published" block, tag chips and a subtitle, which is clutter.
Filenames carry the date, and the sidebar sorts on filename, so ordering is
unaffected.

NO RESTATED QUESTION, AND NO SETUP LINE. The title is the question; the callouts
carry the conditions. A sentence saying what was run before the reader reaches
the answer is throat-clearing.

THREE WORD BUDGETS, ALL LINTED.
  100  words of prose per entry — hero label, answer, warnings, an assembly
       section: everything addressed to the reader, added up.
   50  words per figure caption.
   10  words per Specified/Assumed item. Attribution goes in a preamble line
       above the list, not inside every item.
An inline expression counts as one word.

ORDER MATTERS. Compute cell, hero, answer, callouts, evidence. The reader should
reach the answer without scrolling past the first code cell; `code-fold`
collapses that cell to a single line.

ONE HERO, OR NONE. `.hero` carries the single value the entry exists to produce.
Use `.hero-pair` when the answer IS a comparison (measured vs predicted,
as-built vs as-designed). Use NOTHING when the answer is a figure, a yes/no, or
a number nobody asked for -- a hero that isn't the answer to the title tells the
reader to look at the wrong thing.

NUMBERS IN PROSE ARE INLINE EXPRESSIONS, always. `{python} f"{value:.2f}"`.
This is not a style preference: hand-typed numbers drift from the cells above
them, and the drift is invisible until someone re-derives the result.

DON'T PRINT WORKING. Intermediates (a fit slope, a Reynolds number you already
stated, an all-up mass nobody asked for) are clutter. Print results.

SHOW THE MACHINERY YOU CALLED. An entry that calls shared machinery without
rendering it has stopped documenting its own method. show_source() reads the
source off the live object, so it cannot drift from what ran.

A CELL RETURNING AN OBJECT dumps its repr as a second output and demotes the
figure to a subfigure. Bind it: `_ = bfg.draw_three_view(show=True)`.
-->
